title: Algorithmic Guarantees for Distilling Supervised and Offline RL Datasets
claim: Our synthetic dataset matches full-data test loss and beats random subsets, with the gap shrinking as synthetic dataset size grows.
layout: 3 panels in a row, each a line plot of test loss vs synthetic size with error bars, shared legend per panel
description: Three side-by-side line plots, one per dataset: Red Wine Quality, White Wine Quality and Boston Housing. The x-axis is N_syn (20, 50, 100) and the y-axis is test loss. Each panel has four colored lines with error bars. D_train is blue and flat, marking the full-data baseline. D_rand is orange and starts very high at N_syn=20, with a large error bar, then falls. D_syn is green and D_lev is red. Both sit between the random baseline and the full-data line. All curves converge toward the D_train line as N_syn grows. The legend is in the upper right of each panel, and the grid is light gray. The eye goes first to the steep orange drop and the large error bar at N_syn=20.
caption: MSE Test losses for Homogeneous Linear Regression on the following supervised datasets: red wine quality, white wine quality, Boston Housing.
abstract: Given a training dataset, the goal of dataset distillation is to derive a synthetic dataset such that models trained on the latter perform as well as those trained on the training dataset. In this work, we develop and analyze an efficient dataset distillation algorithm for supervised learning, specifically regression in $\mathbb{R}^d$, based on matching the losses on the training and synthetic datasets with respect to a fixed set of randomly sampled regressors without any model training. Our first key contribution is a novel performance guarantee proving that our algorithm needs only $\tilde{O}(d^2)$ sampled regressors to derive a synthetic dataset on which the MSE loss of any bounded linear model is nearly the same as its MSE loss on the given training data. In particular, the model optimized on the synthetic data has close to minimum loss on the training data, thus performing nearly as well as the model optimized on the latter. Complementing this, we also prove a matching lower bound of $Î©(d^2)$ for the number of sampled regressors showing the tightness of our analysis. Our second contribution is to extend our algorithm to offline RL dataset distillation by matching the Bellman loss, unlike previous works which used a behavioral cloning objective. This is the first such method which leverages both, the rewards and the next state information, available in offline RL datasets, without any policy model optimization. Our algorithm generates a synthetic dataset whose Bellman loss with respect to any linear action-value predictor is close to the latter's Bellman loss on the offline RL training dataset. Therefore, a policy associated with an action-value predictor optimized on the synthetic dataset performs nearly as well as that derived from the one optimized on the training data. We conduct experiments to validate our theoretical guarantees and observe performance gains.
